title: What is Cannabis POS Software?
summary: Cannabis POS software is the compliance, inventory, and sales engine behind a dispensary. What it does, how it differs from retail POS, and what to look for.
body_markdown:
Cannabis POS software is the point-of-sale system built for licensed dispensaries. Beyond ringing up sales, it reports every transaction to the state's track-and-trace system, enforces purchase limits, calculates layered cannabis taxes, and keeps inventory in sync across in-store, online, and delivery orders.


Whether you're opening your first dispensary, running a delivery operation, or expanding to multiple locations, the software you choose can make or break your business. Cannabis-specific POS software isn't just a payment system. It's your compliance engine, inventory manager, customer relationship tool, and operational command center.


**This guide breaks down what cannabis POS software does, how it differs from a traditional retail POS, and what to look for when choosing the[best dispensary POS system](https://getmeadow.com/blog/best-dispensary-pos) for your business.**

## What is Cannabis POS Software?


Cannabis POS software, also called a dispensary POS system or cannabis point of sale, is a specialized tool built for the unique needs of licensed cannabis retailers. It goes far beyond basic payment processing, helping operators manage everything from compliance reporting to customer loyalty programs.


Unlike generic POS systems, cannabis software must handle complex regulatory, inventory, and tax requirements, and stay in sync with state tracking systems like[Metrc](https://getmeadow.com/features/metrc-compliance) .


### How is Cannabis POS Different from Traditional POS?


Cannabis POS differs from a traditional retail POS because it has to enforce state cannabis law at the register: track-and-trace reporting, purchase limits, age verification, and layered cannabis taxes. Cannabis operations also face constant regulatory change, and traditional POS systems aren't built for that level of complexity.


Cannabis-specific POS software is designed to:


- Track and report transactions to state-mandated systems like Metrc
- Manage cannabis-specific products with compliant tracking and labeling
- Enforce purchase limits and age verification
- Apply cannabis-specific tax rates and tax compounding
- Support compliant sales channels, including[delivery](https://getmeadow.com/blog/cannabis-delivery-guide) , curbside, and consumption lounges where they're legal


Here's how the two compare on the requirements that matter most in a dispensary:


*Cannabis POS vs. traditional retail POS, October 2026*


Requirement Traditional retail POS Cannabis POS


State track-and-trace reporting (Metrc) Not supported Reports every sale and adjustment to the state system automatically


Purchase limits Not tracked Enforced by customer and product type


Age verification Optional or manual Built into every transaction


Taxes Standard sales tax Layered excise, state, and local taxes, including compounding


Inventory tracking Counts by SKU Tracks each package by its state-issued tag


Audit trail Basic transaction history Audit-ready log of every sale, adjustment, and user action

Cannabis retail requires a specialized POS because a compliance mistake costs far more than it does in other retail: regulations vary by state, and noncompliance can mean fines, shutdowns, or loss of license. ## 9 Core Features of Cannabis POS Software


Cannabis POS software handles nine core jobs, from track-and-trace reporting to staff permissions. Every operation is different, but a dispensary or delivery service missing any of these will feel it in compliance risk, lost sales, or extra manual work. To score vendors against each one, use the 12-point scorecard in our[guide to choosing a cannabis dispensary POS](https://getmeadow.com/blog/guide-to-choosing-a-cannabis-dispensary-pos-system) .


### 1. Compliance & Track and Trace Integration


Track-and-trace integration connects the POS to the state's seed-to-sale system, so every sale, adjustment, and transfer reports automatically instead of by hand.


- Automatic reporting to your state's track-and-trace system, such as Metrc, with nothing entered by hand
- Active account monitoring to confirm packages upload correctly and to fix any false negatives
- Hands-on Metrc support and training
- Accurate UID labeling


👉[Metrc reporting for dispensaries: what you need to know](https://getmeadow.com/blog/metrc-reporting-for-dispensaries)


👉 See how Meadow handles[Metrc compliance](https://getmeadow.com/features/metrc-compliance)


### 2. Omnichannel Sales


Omnichannel sales lets a dispensary sell in-store, online, through delivery, and at events from one system, with one inventory count behind every channel.


- Unified sales across all channels: in-store, online, delivery, pickup, kiosk, lounges, and events
- Support for dispensary sales models, including traditional counter service, open-floor layouts, floating budtenders, self-serve kiosks, and lounges
- Centralized inventory and compliance tracking no matter where the sale happens
- Real-time syncing across all platforms to avoid overselling or compliance errors

- Product order forecasting and analytics
